question: The Chandela dynasty of Rajput clan ruled which of the following regions between 9th and 13th century in early medieval period of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bundelkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chandela dynasty, belonging to the Rajput clan, ruled the region of **Bundelkhand** in present-day Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh during the 9th to 13th century CE.
 
• The Chandelas are renowned for their significant contributions to architecture, particularly the **Khajuraho group of temples**, which are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
 
• They ruled from their capital at **Khajuraho** and later at Mahoba, showcasing their administrative and cultural prowess.
 
• The Chandela rulers were initially vassals of the Pratiharas but later established their independent rule in the region.
 
• Key rulers of the dynasty include **Yashovarman** and **Dhangadeva**, who were instrumental in expanding and consolidating the Chandela kingdom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bundelkhand Region:**

 
 
• Bundelkhand spans parts of present-day Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh in central India.
 
• The region is known for its rugged terrain and historical significance in Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Khajuraho Temples:**
 
 
• Built by the Chandela rulers, these temples are known for their intricate carvings and sculptures representing various aspects of life, spirituality, and art.
 
• The temples primarily belong to the Hindu and Jain traditions, reflecting the religious harmony of the era.
 
 
 
• **Chandela Dynasty Highlights:**
 
 
• The Chandelas were patrons of art and architecture, leaving behind an enduring legacy through their monuments.
 
• Their rule was marked by a blend of military strength and cultural achievements.
 
 
 
• **End of Chandela Rule:**
 
 
• The dynasty declined after the 13th century due to invasions by the Delhi Sultanate and internal conflicts.
 
• Despite their decline, the Chandelas left an indelible mark on Indian history through their contributions to art and architecture.
